title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Embed, Rerank, and Parse: Advancing Agents with World-Class Retrieval Models
gist: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Embed (8B/1B/1B-NVFP4), Rerank 8B and Parse 631M as open, commercially available retrieval models, claiming #1 on ViDoRe v3.1 dense retrieval, the new ViDoRe v3.1 reranking leaderboard and ParseBench (<1B). The pitch is that better retrieval cuts agent token spend (~13-14% per query with reranking), with NVFP4 and NIM serving numbers aimed at production scale.

themes.theme: Retrieval quality as agent cost lever

insights.claim: NVIDIA frames retrieval quality as a direct driver of agent inference cost: poor evidence makes agents repeat searches and inspect more documents, burning tokens.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Positions retrieval models as an LLM-cost-reduction product, not just an accuracy upgrade, which supports enterprise spend on the retrieval layer.
insights.quote: Better retrieval can help agents reach grounded answers with fewer wasted tokens.

insights.claim: With the agent LLM, tools, tasks and corpus held fixed, adding Nemotron 3.5 Rerank cut agentic token cost per query by about 14% with Embed 8B and 13% with Embed 1B while also improving retrieval accuracy.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Savings are vendor-measured and modest (low-teens percent), so the reranker pays back mainly where agent token volume is large.
insights.locator: Better Retrieval for More Efficient Agents

insights.claim: With Embed 8B as retriever, Nemotron 3.5 Rerank scored about 0.9 nDCG@10 points above Qwen3-VL-Reranker-8B at similar agentic token cost, a small margin over the main open competitor.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Edge over Qwen is thin; model choice may hinge on serving stack and licensing rather than accuracy.
insights.locator: Better Retrieval for More Efficient Agents

insights.claim: Nemotron 3.5 Embed 8B BF16 scored 61.17 nDCG@10 on ViDoRe v3.1, first among dense retrievers and 8.94 points above the prior Llama Nemotron Embed VL 1B at 52.23.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: A near-9 point generational jump on visual document retrieval indicates fast progress in searching charts and tables without OCR.
insights.locator: Leading Multimodal Dense Retrieval on ViDoRe v3

insights.claim: The 1B Embed model distilled from the 8B teacher scores 58.38 nDCG@10 on ViDoRe v3.1, retaining 95.4% of the teacher's score at a much smaller footprint.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Distillation retains most multimodal quality, weakening the case for paying for 8B-class serving in most indexing workloads.
insights.locator: Leading Multimodal Dense Retrieval on ViDoRe v3

insights.claim: On MIRACL Vision the 8B embedder reaches 72.6 nDCG@10, 4.3 points above Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B, and both sizes beat Qwen baselines on KoViDoRe with combined image and text inputs.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Multilingual visual retrieval is a differentiator versus Qwen in non-English enterprise markets.
insights.locator: Leading Multimodal Dense Retrieval on ViDoRe v3

insights.claim: NVIDIA and the MTEB team launched a ViDoRe v3.1 reranking leaderboard, where Nemotron 3.5 Rerank 8B scores 60.49 nDCG@10 on combined inputs versus 59.17 for Qwen-3-VL-Reranker-8B.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: NVIDIA helped create the leaderboard it leads, so treat first-place claims as partly self-defined.
insights.locator: Reranking the Evidence for Agent Tasks

insights.claim: Because the language component is frozen in embedding training, text-only embeddings should stay identical to Nemotron 3 Embed, so existing text vector indexes can be reused.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Lowers migration cost: upgrading to multimodal need not force a re-embed of existing text corpora.
insights.quote: Text-only embeddings are therefore expected to remain unchanged from the corresponding Nemotron 3 Embed models
insights.locator: How We Built the Embed and Rerank Models

insights.claim: On NVIDIA GB200, the NVFP4 1B embedder raises throughput 27.1% (101.3 to 128.8 documents per second) over BF16 while keeping 99.85% of ViDoRe v3 accuracy.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Low-precision quantization is nearly free on embedders, reinforcing the value of Blackwell-class hardware for indexing at scale.

insights.claim: On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, NVIDIA NIM served 6,031 query requests per second versus 2,099 for a comparable vLLM setup, about 2.9x, with similar passage throughput.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: The comparison is vendor-run and query-side only; it supports NIM as a monetizable enterprise layer over open weights.

insights.claim: Fine-tuning for one epoch on synthetic queries raised nDCG@10 for the 1B embedder from 37.34 to 44.12 (18% relative) but the 8B only from 41.44 to 42.75 (3%), so smaller models benefit far more from domain adaptation.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: A tuned 1B can close much of the gap to a generic 8B on niche chart/infographic corpora, favoring cheaper deployments for specialized firms.

insights.claim: Nemotron 3.5 Parse (631M) ranks first on ParseBench among sub-1B models at 75.20 and 10.5 pages per second on one H100; single pass gives 72.74 at 16.1 pages per second, so accuracy can be traded for throughput.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Tunable multi-pass parsing lets firms match cost to document value, pressuring paid OCR/document-AI APIs.
insights.locator: Leading Accuracy with Faster Document Processing

insights.claim: Post-training Parse with GRPO and custom rewards is meant to reduce repetitive generation loops and unclosed blocks and improve table consistency.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Reinforcement learning is spreading from reasoning models to structured-output reliability in perception pipelines.

insights.claim: Vectorize reports Nemotron 3.5 Embed ranked first on LoCoMo (93.8% recall@10) and BEAM 100K (65.9%) against seven other embedders, pointing to use in agent memory.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Agent memory is emerging as a distinct retrieval workload where embedding choice matters.

insights.claim: Turbopuffer found Embed 8B gave about 5% more relevant results at Recall@20 than the next best model on an enterprise PDF benchmark, and Perplexity found Rerank 8B had the highest average on its private 72-task reranking benchmark.
insights.speaker: Yauhen Babakhin
insights.so_what: Adoption by search and vector-DB vendors and distribution via Baseten, DeepInfra, FriendliAI and OpenRouter points to NVIDIA moving up the stack from GPUs into retrieval models.
